sections.title: Daily contracts
bullets: Claiming a finished daily contract now also gives 200 GP on top of its credits. The contract card still shows only the credits; the GP appears in your balance.

sections.title: General
bullets: New players start with 10000 GP.

sections.title: Team Deathmatch
bullets: With the 40-per-team setting, bots can now fill a side past 24 players.
With a team size set (now 20), each side fills with bots up to it.

sections.title: Social
bullets: Server chat messages about players online and players searching for a match now show the time in your local time and format. Requires the new launcher; older launchers will display UTC.

sections.title: Proving Grounds
bullets: Back to the normal Proving Grounds — you start in your own ships again instead of in a fighter.

sections.title: Escalation
bullets: **Escalation** is off the queues for now. Before, it was playable from the Proving Grounds button.

sections.title: Escalation
bullets: Losing your ship drops you two levels down the ladder instead of all the way back to a fighter, and dreadnoughts are now their own top level at 500 points.

sections.title: Market
bullets: The store loads faster: the catalog is packed the way the game itself unpacks it.

sections.title: Conquest
bullets: Claimed territory now draws on every player's screen.

sections.title: Escalation
bullets: **Escalation** is here: a Team Deathmatch where everyone starts in a fighter and unlocks bigger ship classes as their match score grows. It runs on the TDM maps, queued from the Proving Grounds button.

sections.title: Market
bullets: Coatings, decals and emblems are buyable in the ship customizer.
The **Halloween sale** is live, run through the game's own campaign system.
Per-class cosmetic offers are slimmer so the store stays inside the game's own download limit. Before, the store could stall for minutes.

sections.title: General
bullets: Custom games have lobby rooms again.

sections.title: Conquest
bullets: Capture points are in place before the match starts.

sections.title: Hangar
bullets: Contracts load correctly and refresh after you log in.

sections.title: General
bullets: The rewards page shows again after your first match. Before, it stayed hidden.

sections.title: Team Elimination
bullets: The round banner appears once the result is actually shown, and you get your own pick when every side start is blocked.

sections.title: Hangar
bullets: Captains: empty appearance slots are filled, and the **Standard Issue** outfit is free.

sections.title: Onslaught
bullets: Command Ship abilities fire reliably. Before, an ability could fail to register.

sections.title: Hangar
bullets: Daily contracts pay out when you claim them.

sections.title: Tech tree
bullets: Hero ships keep their XP when their hull is shared with a regular ship.

sections.title: Team Deathmatch
bullets: Adds **Elysium (Paradise)**, **Ryugu Haven (Space02)** and **Amirani**.

sections.title: Team Elimination
bullets: Sides, fighter starts, ready-up and a team HUD — and the first-kill crash is fixed.

sections.title: Conquest
bullets: Plays by the original rules: captured points claim territory, spawns sit at capture points, and everyone sees the territory update.

sections.title: Onslaught
bullets: Adds **Elysium (Paradise)** and Command Ship abilities.

sections.title: Ceres Awakens
bullets: Tech-cache pickups score and pay credits, and a cache's buff ends when its collector is destroyed.

sections.title: Havoc
bullets: Fighters fly while you are eliminated, and wave 1 never has modifiers.

sections.title: General
bullets: Hero ships report their XP under their own loadout, and ships you unlock mid-session get their XP.

sections.title: Team Elimination
bullets: Rounds are best of 3, and you drop to fighters after a lost ship.

sections.title: Launcher
bullets: The launcher gets the original launcher's look, resolves the server on every Play, and scales for your display.

sections.title: Market
bullets: Store images load reliably.

sections.title: Tech tree
bullets: Ship pages show the next ships and the briefing; fitted items no longer sit under the wrong line.

sections.title: Havoc
bullets: HUD feeds and the ready flag work, and the end screen lists your rewards.

sections.title: Havoc
bullets: **Wave mode** is here, built from the game's own rules and data.
Team HUD; **Junkyard Prince** is unlockable; modifiers only apply to live ships.

sections.title: General
bullets: Leaderboards and the in-match ribbon popup work.

sections.title: Market
bullets: The store's catalog downloads in one piece again — the game could not read the compressed version.

sections.title: General
bullets: Statistics, live ribbons, the scoring table and hangar names work.

sections.title: Hangar
bullets: Loadout saves confirm, and hero fits are owned.

sections.title: Tech tree
bullets: After you research a module, its credit price shows up without restarting the game.

sections.title: Onslaught
bullets: Veteran and Legendary Command Ship guns fire properly, and bots target Command Ships.
Onslaught joins the regular map rotation.

sections.title: All game modes
bullets: Bots wait for the match to start instead of moving during the countdown.

sections.title: Hangar
bullets: Career progression is rebuilt and contract activation times run correctly.
Daily contracts are here — three plus an elite, with progress from your match results, credit payouts and rerolls.

sections.title: Market
bullets: Heroes and owned ships lend their hull parts to their line; uncustomised ships wear their own look.

sections.title: General
bullets: PvE matches run Season 1 events from the game's own tables.
The statistics screen no longer crashes; inventory and Elite status refresh in-session, and the original ribbons are back.

sections.title: Conquest
bullets: Team scores and capture points work — points activate at match start and the scores update as the match runs.

sections.title: Onslaught
bullets: AI ships move.

sections.title: Ceres Awakens
bullets: The queue called PodTDM is really **Ceres Awakens** — its buff pods live on Ryugu Haven (Space02). Before, it was announced as Team Deathmatch.

sections.title: Conquest
bullets: Only on Territory maps; mode names in chat.

sections.title: Onslaught
bullets: Onslaught points, AI ships and the original match XP.

sections.title: All game modes
bullets: Scoring uses the original per-mode table, and match XP counts your in-match events.

sections.title: Hangar
bullets: **LOADOUT B** — a second loadout per ship.

sections.title: Market
bullets: Other ships' blueprint hulls are no longer granted or sold.

sections.title: Hangar
bullets: Flagships use the ship's own loadout slot.

sections.title: Market
bullets: Cosmetic ownership in the forms the game checks; free items and templates.

sections.title: Social
bullets: Chat rooms, direct messages, solo squads and a profanity filter.

sections.title: Hangar
bullets: Flagships are stored and applied; bought heroes reach the client.

sections.title: Market
bullets: Owning a ship owns its blueprint look.

sections.title: Tech tree
bullets: The next-ship gate counts the modules the game counts.

sections.title: Social
bullets: Chat only announces queues that are still open.

sections.title: General
bullets: Match results say team names, not 'T'.
The matchmaker can backfill running matches.

sections.title: General
bullets: Hero ships report their own tier.
Matches start once the host's game mode is running.
Clients that failed the secure handshake connect via a compatibility fallback.

sections.title: Market
bullets: The original bundles — **Rogue Cache**, **Renegade Stash** and the rest — replace the empty placeholders in the store.
Ship cosmetics sort into their own vanity sections, and hero ships are offered for points (our estimated prices).

sections.title: Tech tree
bullets: Officer briefings join the tech tree — the four 101 briefings come with any tier III–V ship, and each of the other 16 belongs to one specific ship. Before, no tree carried a briefing at all.

sections.title: General
bullets: Match rewards use the fleet of the match's type — Veteran and Legendary matches no longer fall back to the Recruit fleet.
